observations: Photo 0: A white smartphone with a triple-camera setup and a large square cutout on the back, held in hand. The phone has a white case or back cover with no visible branding. Background shows a sign with 'HAMWALBAL ENTERPRISE' and a logo with phones.

Photo 1: The same phone shown next to its open box. The box has a printed image of a white iPhone with a triple-camera setup and an Apple logo. The phone matches the image in the box. The box appears to be for an iPhone, but no model name is visible.

Photo 2: A screenshot of the phone's 'About' section showing: Capacity 256 GB, Available 235.96 GB, Wi-Fi Address, Bluetooth, Modem Firmware 2.10.01, SFID, EID, Network Provider Lock: No SIM restrictions. The phone has a notch at the top of the screen, typical of iPhones. The time shown is 08:13. The screen is bright and clear.

The phone in the photos does not match any known iPhone 17 Pro model. The iPhone 17 Pro has not been released as of 2024. The design shown is more consistent with an iPhone 14 Pro or 15 Pro, which have a triple-camera setup and a notch.

read_from: photo 2 screen: 'About' section shows 256GB capacity and 'No SIM restrictions'
photo 1 box: Apple logo and iPhone-style design

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and 1: The phone's design (triple-camera layout, notch) matches iPhone 14 Pro or 15 Pro, not the non-existent iPhone 17 Pro. No iPhone 17 Pro has been released. The box in photo 1 does not show 'iPhone 17 Pro'.

Photo 2: 'About' screen shows 'No SIM restrictions' and 'Available SIMs' but does not confirm physical eSIM capability. The term 'Physical Esim' is misleading; eSIM is digital. The phone likely supports eSIM, but the claim is phrased incorrectly.

Photos show the phone and box, but no close-up of the phone's screen, edges, or buttons to verify condition. The box is open, but no damage is visible. The term 'neatly used' is subjective and not proven.

risks.risk: The phone is not an iPhone 17 Pro, but a different model (likely iPhone 14 Pro or 15 Pro), which affects value.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the phone's front screen showing the model name in Settings > General > About, or a photo of the box with the model name printed.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic 256GB iPhone without model, which is lower than a true iPhone 17 Pro (if it existed).

risks.risk: The phone may be stolen, blacklisted, or have a compromised EID/IMEI.
risks.proof: A video showing the phone being powered on, with the Settings > General > About screen clearly visible, including the IMEI/EID, and a check via a Nigerian carrier or IMEI checker.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially blacklisted or compromised, which reduces value significantly.

risks.risk: The phone may have screen damage, dead pixels, or hardware issues not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the phone being used: swiping, opening apps, checking camera, and a close-up of the screen under different lighting.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as possibly defective, which reduces value.

proof_requests: A clear photo or video of the phone's Settings > General > About screen showing the exact model name (e.g., iPhone 14 Pro).
A video showing the phone being powered on and used, including camera and screen functionality.
A photo of the original box with the model name printed on it, if available.
response.reason: The seller claims an iPhone 17 Pro, which does not exist, contradicting the visual evidence. The phone appears to be an iPhone 14 Pro or 15 Pro. The model must be confirmed to price correctly. Hidden risks include blacklisting and hardware defects, which require further proof to assess.
